channel.title: TheSocialPundit Journal
channel.description: Practical guides on personal branding, thought leadership, LinkedIn strategy and using AI for professional content.

item.title: How to Build a Personal Brand as a Professional: A Practical Guide
item.description: To build a personal brand as a professional, pick a narrow area of expertise, develop a clear point of view on it, and share that view consistently where your audience already pays attention, usually LinkedIn. Your brand is the pattern people notice across many useful posts, not any single one.

item.title: How to Become a Thought Leader in Your Industry
item.description: You become a thought leader by consistently publishing original, useful perspectives on a focused topic, grounded in real experience and current events. Recognition follows when people repeatedly find your thinking helpful, so focus on being useful and specific rather than on appearing important.

item.title: How to Use AI to Write LinkedIn Posts That Still Sound Like You
item.description: Use AI for the legwork, not the thinking. Give it a real source and your own angle, ask for a structured draft, then edit until every claim is accurate and every sentence sounds like you. Never publish an AI draft you haven't reviewed line by line.

item.title: How to Turn Industry News into LinkedIn Posts People Actually Read
item.description: Don't just share the link. Pick a story your audience cares about, add your interpretation (what it means, who it affects and what to do about it), and lead with that insight rather than the headline. One clear take on timely news is one of the most reliable ways to build authority on LinkedIn.

item.title: LinkedIn Content Strategy for Executives: What Business Leaders Should Post
item.description: An effective executive LinkedIn strategy rests on three or four recurring themes tied to your company's direction, a sustainable rhythm of two or three posts a week, and content that shows judgment: perspectives on your industry, lessons from leadership decisions and honest views on what is changing. Keep the ideas yours, even if you get help with the writing.

item.title: How Often Should Professionals Post on LinkedIn?
item.description: For most professionals, two to three quality posts a week is a strong, sustainable target, and even one a week works if you keep it up. Consistency over months matters far more than posting daily for a few weeks, and a weaker post published just to fill a schedule does more harm than skipping a day.

item.title: How to Repurpose Articles into Social Media Posts (Without Repeating Yourself)
item.description: To repurpose an article, pull out its distinct ideas, such as a key finding, a contrarian point, a practical step or a story, and turn each into its own post, adapted to the format of each network. One strong article can become a week or more of content without anything feeling repetitive.

item.title: 10 Personal Branding Mistakes Professionals Should Avoid
item.description: The biggest personal branding mistakes are being too broad, posting inconsistently, sharing without a point of view, over-promoting, and publishing generic or unchecked AI content. Fix them by narrowing your focus, keeping a sustainable rhythm and making every post useful and unmistakably yours.

item.title: How to Stay Updated on Industry Trends (Without Drowning in News)
item.description: Stay updated by following a small, trusted set of sources for your specific field, filtering ruthlessly for relevance, and reviewing them in a short, fixed daily or weekly slot. Then capture your reactions, because the professionals who stand out don't just consume trends, they interpret them in public.

item.title: How to Develop a Professional Point of View People Remember
item.description: A professional point of view is a clear, defensible position on how your field works or should work, drawn from your experience. Develop one by listing the beliefs you hold that thoughtful peers might dispute, testing them against evidence, and expressing them consistently when relevant news gives you an opening.

item.title: One Voice, Ten Platforms: A Practical Guide to Multi-Platform Posting
item.description: Your audience isn't only on LinkedIn anymore. Here's how to show up consistently on ten platforms without sounding like ten different people.

item.title: The 15-Minute Content Calendar for Busy Professionals
item.description: You don't need a content team to post consistently. You need a repeatable 15-minute weekly ritual — here's exactly what it looks like.

item.title: Can AI-Generated Posts Still Sound Like You? What We Learned Building TheSocialPundit
item.description: Generic AI content is easy to spot and easy to ignore. Here's the difference between AI that writes for you and AI that writes as you.

item.title: What Changed in the LinkedIn Algorithm in 2026 (And What Didn't)
item.description: Dwell time matters more than ever, external links are still quietly penalized, and comments in the first hour remain the single biggest lever.

item.title: Why Generic AI Content Fails — And How Industry Curation Fixes It
item.description: "Write me a post about AI" produces content anyone could have written. The fix isn't a better prompt — it's better source material.

item.title: Personal Brand vs. Company Brand: Why Executives Need Both
item.description: A strong company page builds trust in the business. A strong personal voice builds trust in the people running it. Neither replaces the other.

item.title: Beyond LinkedIn: Should Professionals Post on Reddit and Mastodon?
item.description: Different platforms, different unwritten rules. Here's how to tell when a channel is worth your time — and how to not get banned in week one.

item.title: Why Consistency Beats Virality for Professional Branding
item.description: One viral post gets you a week of attention. Fifty ordinary posts over a year get you a reputation. Only one of those compounds.
